surviver

surviver estimates vaccine effectiveness as a function of time since vaccination, VE(t), from individual-level data on vaccination and reported infections.

It combines survival analysis with infectious disease modelling. Each person’s hazard of infection is driven by the force of infection they are exposed to, built from daily prevalence and an age-structured contact matrix, and vaccination modifies that hazard by a log hazard ratio γ(t) that varies smoothly with time since vaccination:

log⁡h=log⁡β+log⁡I‾(tc,a)+γ(t)V,VE(t)=1−eγ(t) \log h = \log\beta + \log \bar I(t_c, a) + \gamma(t)\,V, \qquad \mathrm{VE}(t) = 1 - e^{\gamma(t)}

The model is a Poisson approximation to a Cox model, fitted in Stan with a random-walk prior on γ(t), so VE can rise, plateau and wane without assuming a functional form.

The method was developed by Group D at the Lorentz Center workshop Connecting Survival Analysis and Infectious Disease Modelling (Leiden, June 2026).

Status: experimental. The method is under active development and validation. See the lab notebook for what has been checked so far and the known open issues.

Installation 

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("kylieainslie/surviver")

Fitting models needs cmdstanr and CmdStan, which are not on CRAN:

install.packages("cmdstanr", repos = c("https://stan-dev.r-universe.dev", getOption("repos")))
cmdstanr::install_cmdstan()

Example

Estimate VE(t) from a simulated dataset where the true VE is known:

library(surviver)

# person-level data: demographics, vaccination and reported cases
pop <- ve_population(ve_sim_waning)

# force of infection by day and age group, from reported cases
inc  <- daily_incidence(pop)
prev <- daily_prevalence(inc, duration_infection = 7, reporting_delay = 2)
foi  <- force_of_infection(prev, age_group_sizes(pop), contact_matrix = polymod_nl)

# person-days split at vaccination, aggregated for Stan
pd <- expand_person_days(counting_process(pop))
sd <- make_stan_data(pd, foi)

# fit and plot against the true curve
fit <- fit_ve(sd, seed = 42)
ve  <- extract_ve(fit)
plot_ve(ve, truth = ve_sim_waning$params)

To use your own data, pass ve_population() a folder containing demographic_data.rds, vaccination_data.rds and incidence_data_reduced.rds, or a list with demographic, vaccination and incidence data frames (see ?ve_population).

Main functions

Step Functions
Prepare data ve_population(), sample_cohort(), add_age_group()
Exposure daily_incidence(), daily_prevalence(), force_of_infection(), age_group_sizes()
Survival data counting_process(), expand_person_days(), make_stan_data()
Fit and summarise fit_ve(), extract_ve(), plot_ve()
Validation true_ve(), simulate_counts(), contact_matrix_hermes()

Two Stan models are bundled (ve_stan_file()): "noncentered" (default) and "centered" parameterisations of the random walk.

Data

Dataset Description
ve_sim_waning Simulated outbreak, 10,000 people, 180 days. VE rises to 0.8 over 14 days, then wanes (half-life 45 days) towards 0.1
ve_sim_no_waning As above, but VE stays at 0.8 after the ramp
polymod_nl POLYMOD contact matrix for the Netherlands, five age groups

The simulated datasets were generated with the HERMES individual-based model (household, school, workplace and community transmission), extended with waning vaccine protection. The script is data-raw/ve_test_scenarios.R; it needs a local clone of HERMES (set HERMES_PATH), and each dataset records the HERMES commit it came from.
